quotes.quote: The Cyber Index is an equally weighted average of its three evaluations.

CWE-Bench-AA is Artificial Analysis' implementation of Collinear AI's CWE-bench, a defensive cybersecurity benchmark that evaluates coding agents on auditing open-source codebases for security weaknesses and patching them without breaking legitimate behavior.
DeepsecBench-AA is our implementation of Vercel's DeepsecBench, a benchmark that measures how well models find vulnerabilities in application code.

CyberGym-E2E-AA is our implementation of CyberGym-E2E, from the Berkeley Center for Responsible, Decentralized Intelligence (RDI), which tests the full defensive loop on real memory-safety vulnerabilities.
It does not cover incident response, writing new code without introducing vulnerabilities, targets without source access such as compiled software or live servers, or exploit realization.
Launched the Artificial Analysis Cyber Index with three evaluations, each weighted 1/3: CWE-Bench-AA, DeepsecBench-AA, and CyberGym-E2E-AA
We record cases where a model or provider declines a task on safety grounds and report them separately from the score.
The evaluation set is 120 held-out tasks, private to Collinear AI and Artificial Analysis.
Share of the 120 held-out CWE-bench tasks a model solves on a single attempt.
GPT-6 Luna (Max) has the lowest cost per task on CWE-Bench-AA, at $0.11, followed by Beam 1.0 at $0.15 and MiMo-V2.6-Pro at $0.18
All evaluations are conducted independently by Artificial Analysis.
The evaluation is private, scoring findings against a golden set of vulnerabilities and bugs verified by human experts.
GPT-6 Sol (Max) scores the highest on DeepsecBench-AA F2 with a score of 46%, followed by GPT-6 Astra (Max) with a score of 37% and Kimi K3.1 Pro with a score of 37%
Mistral Large 4 (Medium) has the lowest cost per task on DeepsecBench-AA, at $0.0589, followed by Beam 1.0 at $0.0807 and GPT-6 Luna (Max) at $0.0825
The original dataset contains 920 vulnerabilities across 139 open-source projects, drawn from Google's OSS-Fuzz.
Kimi K3.1 Pro scores the highest on CyberGym-E2E-AA pass@1 with a score of 95%, followed by Mistral Large 4 Preview with a score of 82% and Mistral Large 4 (High) with a score of 79%
GPT-6 Luna (Max) has the lowest cost per task on CyberGym-E2E-AA, at $0.13, followed by DeepSeek V4.1 Flash (Max) at $0.16 and MiMo-V2.6-Pro at $0.20

It is a standalone index of model capability on cyber defense, and combines evaluation datasets from industry partners and academia to measure how well a model can support and accelerate the work of an internal security team.
Developer of CWE-bench, contributed as a private held-out evaluation.
Exploit realization, turning a found vulnerability into a working exploit, is out of scope for a defense-focused index.
Because cyber work is dual-use, we also track cases where a model or provider declines a task on safety grounds, and report them separately from the score.
Security teams face the same open-ended problem: deciding where to look in a large codebase that keeps changing.
Given the open-ended nature of DeepsecBench-AA, it is unsurprising that not all vulnerabilities are found, with the best model identifying only 41% of the expert-verified issues.

Refusals are a significant factor on CyberGym-E2E-AA: GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6 Sol, Claude Fable 5.1, Claude Opus 5.5, Qwen3.8 2.4T A95B, and Qwen3.8 27B refuse at least 98% of tasks, making it difficult to assess frontier model performance.
Discovery is the main challenge, with 42% of attempts reaching the 90-minute limit without an input that crashes the program.
We will review the Index as models improve and add evaluations as new capabilities need measuring, starting with the gaps listed above.
September 28, 2026
GPT-6 Sol (Daybreak Blue, max) now leads the Index and sits on the Cost vs. Capability Pareto frontier.
